Simulate a high-speed, compressible supersonic jet discharging from a nozzle into a larger 2D domain using OpenFOAM.
Treat air as a perfect gas.
Use the `rhoCentralFoam` density-based transient compressible solver, set in `system/controlDict` as `application rhoCentralFoam;`.
The mesh is 2D, extruded one cell in the z direction, with the `frontAndBack` patch defined as type `empty`.
The nozzle inlet has a Mach number of 2.0 with fixed supersonic inflow values: `U = (686 0 0) m/s`, `T = 300 K`, `p = 101325 Pa`.
The nozzle exit is a slot with height 0.01 m.
The outer domain extends approximately 0.2 m downstream in x (about 10–20 exit heights) and 0.05–0.1 m in y (about 5–10 exit heights), providing a larger domain than the nozzle.
The jet is perfectly expanded: the ambient far-field is initialized and maintained at `p = 101325 Pa` and `T = 300 K`, matching the nozzle exit static pressure.
In `constant/thermophysicalProperties`, configure `thermoType` with `hePsiThermo`, `equationOfState perfectGas`, and `transport sutherland` using standard air Sutherland coefficients (asymptotic viscosity mu = 1.458e-6, Tref = 273.15 K, S = 110.4 K), with Cv = 718 J/kg/K and Pr = 0.7.
Boundary conditions: nozzle inlet uses `fixedValue` for `U`, `p`, and `T`.
Far-field/outlet boundaries use `waveTransmissive` for `p` and `T` and `zeroGradient` for `U`.
Solid walls use `noSlip` for `U` with matched zero-gradient/adiabatic conditions for `p` and `T`, consistent with the laminar treatment.
Run the case as laminar (no turbulence model) to capture the inviscid-style shock-cell structure (barrel shocks and Mach disk).
Use the standard viscous term (viscous effects active) so `noSlip` walls are consistent.
In `system/controlDict`, set `endTime 0.005`, `writeInterval 0.0005`, `adjustTimeStep yes`, `maxCo 0.5`, and an initial `deltaT` of 1e-7, since `rhoCentralFoam` is explicit and requires CFL-limited time stepping.
Ensure the initial and far-field fields in the `0/` directory are consistent: interior and far-field initialized at `p = 101325 Pa`, `T = 300 K`, `U = (0 0 0)` m/s, with the nozzle inlet patch at the specified supersonic inflow values.
